Business live: FTSE 100 edges higher as pound steadies before Fed decision

Published 2026-10-07 07:30 UTC

Good morning and welcome to our rolling coverage of business, the financial markets and the world economy. Markets are in a holding pattern this morning ahead of two big central bank decisions, and the FTSE 100 has opened slightly higher. This entry exists to test robots.txt handling and should never be fetched by the extractor because the live blog path is disallowed for crawlers.

9.05am BST: Good morning, and welcome to our rolling coverage of business, the financial markets and the world economy. The FTSE 100 has opened slightly higher, up 0.3%, with mining and banking shares leading the way, while the pound is steady against the dollar ahead of tonight's interest rate decision in Washington.

9.40am BST: Housebuilders are among the risers this morning after new figures showed UK house prices rising at their fastest pace in two years. Shares in several big builders are up more than 2%. Analysts say lower mortgage rates are bringing buyers back.

10.15am BST: Oil prices are edging lower, with Brent crude down 0.5%. Energy shares are lagging the wider market as a result. Traders are cautious ahead of the US central bank's announcement, which is expected to include another cut in borrowing costs.

11.30am BST: Retailers are mixed. One high street chain has warned that warm weather hit sales of autumn clothing, sending its shares down 6%. Online fashion companies are also under pressure as investors weigh tougher competition.

1.10pm BST: European stock markets are also higher, with Germany's DAX up 0.4% and France's CAC 40 up 0.2%. The euro is little changed. Bond yields across Europe are slightly lower as investors anticipate easier monetary policy in the US.

2.45pm BST: Wall Street is expected to open flat, as investors wait for the rate decision. We will be covering the announcement and the reaction in markets this evening, so stay with us.
